document_check.note: The document is Vlachos I, Moschovos C, Apostolakopoulou L, Karasavvidou K, Ntanasi E, Mamalaki E, Kugiumtzis D, Kimiskidis VK, Scarmeas N, Kyrozis A. 'Resting EEG partial coherence demonstrates increased gamma range central functional connectivity in amnestic mild cognitive impairment', Brain Research 1867 (2025) 149973, doi 10.1016/j.brainres.2025.149973. It is a single-cohort cross-sectional comparison of resting EEG in 21 amnestic MCI and 62 cognitively normal ALBION participants (Athens). Its title matches the summaries.md block for Paper 368. The cited numbers match the document: the local PCOH cluster p = 0.0290 (EC, 32 to 100 Hz) and p = 0.0272 (EO, 28 to 100 Hz) on p.11, the lCEO cluster p = 0.085 on p.11, and the PSD null on p.6.

cited_result: Local (per-electrode) partial coherence (PCOH) was higher in 21 amnestic MCI than in 62 cognitively normal ALBION participants in cluster-based permutation tests: eyes closed, 32 to 100 Hz, p = 0.0290; eyes open, 28 to 100 Hz, p = 0.0272 (p.11). The comparators were measured in the same participants. Band-averaged PSD 'did not indicate any significant difference' (p.6). Local ordinary coherence formed no cluster with eyes closed, and its eyes-open cluster was not significant (p = 0.085) (pp.10 to 11).
tool_reason: The cited result compares an EEG connectivity measure between diagnostic groups (aMCI against CN), measured once in participants drawn from one clinic cohort. That makes it a single-time-point group comparison, not a prediction model or an accuracy estimate against a reference standard.

domains.domain: Item 1: Criteria for inclusion clearly defined
domains.rationale: The cohort exclusion criteria and the study inclusion criteria are both stated explicitly. Two features limit this without making it unclear. The number of ALBION participants screened is not given. The requirement for the same diagnosis at two consecutive yearly evaluations selects diagnostically stable participants, and 2 unstable cases were excluded. This may widen the contrast between the groups.

signalling.question: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
signalling.quote: In the present study we have included all ALBION participants who satisfied the following criteria

signalling.question: Were the inclusion criteria operationalised (diagnostic stability, EEG timing)?
signalling.quote: They were classified in the same mental status group (either CN or amnestic MCI) in two consecutive yearly clinical evaluations and underwent a quality EEG that included the eyes open −eyes closed protocol within 6 months after the first one of the 2 evaluations.

signalling.question: Were exclusion criteria stated?
signalling.quote: Exclusion criteria are previously established diagnosis of dementia, neurological, psychiatric or medical conditions associated with a high risk of cognitive impairment or dementia, MRI contraindications, as well as the use of anticoagulant medication

signalling.question: Is the number of cohort participants screened or eligible reported?
signalling.quote: Searched Sections 2.1 and 3.1 for the number of ALBION participants screened or with EEG; only the included count is given: 'Criteria were satisfied by 83 subjects, 21 of whom were classified as amnestic MCI and 62 as CN in two consecutive evaluations.'

signalling.question: Were participants excluded after classification?
signalling.quote: Two participants who were classified as MCI in the first evaluation and cognitively normal in the second were excluded from analysis.

domains.domain: Item 2: Study subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: The setting is described: the ALBION cohort at the Aiginition Hospital cognitive disorders clinic, with referral routes, and help-seeking controls who were found cognitively normal. Group demographics (sex, age, education) are tabulated. Group cognitive scores are not tabulated.

signalling.question: Was the setting described?
signalling.quote: ALBION is an on-going, longitudinal study taking place in the Cognitive Disorders Clinic of Aiginition Hospital of the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens.

signalling.question: Was the source of the control group described?
signalling.quote: The control (CN) group included subjects who were assessed in ALBION because of a concern over their memory and cognitive status in general but were found to be cognitively normal in the evaluation preceding the EEG

signalling.question: Are participant characteristics tabulated by group?
signalling.quote: Subject demographics and information.

signalling.question: Are cognitive scores reported by group?
signalling.quote: Searched Table 2 and Section 3.1: only number of subjects, sex, age (median/range) and education (median years/range) are given; no MMSE, ACE-r or domain z-scores by group.

domains.domain: Item 3: Exposure (diagnostic group membership) measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale: Every participant received the same extensive structured assessment. An experienced neurologist assigned the diagnosis using a one-hour neuropsychological battery. Group membership had to be the same at two consecutive yearly evaluations. Biomarker confirmation of AD aetiology is absent, but this does not affect the clinical aMCI against CN classification that the result concerns.

signalling.question: Was cognitive status established with a structured assessment?
signalling.quote: Neuropsychological evaluation was conducted by trained neuropsychologists with an extensive battery of neuropsychological tests, lasting approximately one hour, assessing all major cognitive domains.

signalling.question: Who assigned the diagnosis and on what information?
signalling.quote: an experienced neurologist in the cognitive disorder field evaluated all information provided by the individual, as well as any reliable collateral history, in conjunction with the objective scores from the comprehensive battery of neuropsychological tests.

signalling.question: Were both groups assessed in the same way?
signalling.quote: Each participant undergoes an extensive, structured assessment, including several demographic, medical, social, environmental, clinical, nutritional, neuropsychological determinants and lifestyle activities.

signalling.question: Was reliability of classification addressed?
signalling.quote: The mental status stability criterion was included in order to decrease the possibility of classification bias.

signalling.question: Was the diagnosis supported by AD biomarkers?
signalling.quote: diagnosis was based on clinical, neuropsychologic and routine MRI criteria, without reference to more specific biomarkers, such as Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) amyloid, tau and P-tau, or to amyloid PET imaging.

domains.domain: Item 4: Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition
domains.rationale: MCI is defined operationally: complaint, a deficit of 1.5 SD in at least one domain, no dementia, preserved daily function. Normative z-scores come from non-impaired participants. MRI and neurological examination exclude non-AD causes in the MCI group. The rule assigning the amnestic subtype is not stated. The source of the published criteria is not cited in Methods.

signalling.question: Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition?
signalling.quote: A MCI diagnosis was assigned when the participant reported cognitive complaints and had a measurable deficit in cognition with a standard deviation below 1.5 in at least one domain in the absence of dementia or impairment in everyday functioning.

signalling.question: Were the deficit thresholds referenced to normative data?
signalling.quote: z-scores were derived for each test, using the means and standard deviations (SD) calculated from the scores of participants without dementia and mild cognitive impairment.

signalling.question: Was the rule assigning the amnestic subtype stated?
signalling.quote: Searched Sections 2.1 and 2.2; the only statement is 'The MCI group was further classified into two subgroups, amnestic and non-amnestic MCI.'

signalling.question: Were non-AD causes excluded in the MCI group?
signalling.quote: The neurologic exam and brain MRI of the amnestic MCI patients showed no evidence pointing to a non-AD diagnosis that might cause cognitive decline.

domains.rationale: Age, sex and education are named as confounders. The significant group imbalances in age and education are reported. Cholinesterase-inhibitor use and age are named in the Discussion as factors that affect gamma activity.

signalling.question: Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: linear regression models were used to control for confounder effects due to age, sex and education level of the subjects

signalling.question: Were group imbalances on confounders reported?
signalling.quote: There were statistically significant differences with respect to age (p = 0.001) and education level (p < 0.001)

signalling.question: Were other potential confounders of gamma activity recognised?
signalling.quote: Use of anti-cholinesterase inhibitors, which has been reported to increase γ activity (Fide et al., 2023), may play a role.

domains.domain: Item 6: Strategies to deal with confounding stated
domains.rationale: Regression adjustment for age, sex and education is stated for the group tests, but only as a one-sentence claim with no adjusted estimates shown. The sentence cannot apply literally to every test, since many unadjusted tests were not significant. Nothing says the adjustment was applied to the cluster-based permutation tests that produce the cited p-values. Label permutation does not incorporate covariates unless the data are residualised first. The groups differ by a median of 6 years in age and 5 in education. Medication use, which the authors themselves name as a confounder, is not reported for the sample.

signalling.question: Was a strategy to deal with confounding stated?
signalling.quote: linear regression models were used to control for confounder effects due to age, sex and education level of the subjects, and the adjusted p-values always remained below the statistical significance threshold.

signalling.question: Was the adjustment applied to the cited cluster-based permutation tests?
signalling.quote: Searched Sections 2.4.3 and 3.5 and the Fig. 9 caption; the cluster results (p = 0.0290, p = 0.0272) are reported with no mention of covariate adjustment and no adjusted cluster statistics.

signalling.question: Is the absence of confounding supported by shown data?
signalling.quote: but as mentioned above this did not result in confounding effects for the connectivity analysis.

signalling.question: Was medication use (for example cholinesterase inhibitors) recorded or handled in the sample?
signalling.quote: Searched Sections 2.1, 2.2 and 3.1 for medication use in the sample; it is raised only in the Discussion ('Use of anti-cholinesterase inhibitors ... may play a role').

domains.domain: Item 7: Outcomes (EEG connectivity) measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale:
The recording and the computation of COH and PCOH are fully specified and algorithmic: standard 10-20 montage, 1024 Hz, VAR order 14, 2 s windows. Several threats to validity in the gamma range are not resolved:
- Artefact-free segments were chosen by visual inspection, with no blinding to group reported.
- Eye blinks were retained.
- No EMG-specific removal was done, although the authors state that gamma is vulnerable to tonic EMG.
- The Fpz-area reference is atypical.
- A 50 Hz notch filter was applied inside the 50 to 100 Hz band.
- Artefact-free data were short (2.3 min EO, 3.7 min EC).
- No test-retest reliability of PCOH is reported.
The MCI group had somewhat higher high-frequency power, which fits either a neural or a muscular source. The authors argue that PCOH is insensitive to common-mode artefacts and that the effects are central, away from EMG-prone sites. This mitigates the concern but does not establish validity.

signalling.question: Was the EEG recorded with a standard system and montage?
signalling.quote: EEG was recorded with a 19-channel EEG system (Micromed, amplifier SAM 25FO) placed according to the standard International 10–20 system

signalling.question: Was artefact rejection done blind to diagnostic group?
signalling.quote: data were visually inspected by KK under the supervision of expert EEG examiners AK and CM to identify artifact-free eyes-open (EO) and eyes-closed (EC) periods and annotate their respective starting and ending points.

signalling.question: Were artefacts fully removed?
signalling.quote: Eye blinks were the only artifact that did not lead to exclusion from analysis.

signalling.question: Was enough clean data available per participant?
signalling.quote: The average artifact-free recording duration was 2.3 min for EO and 3.7 min for EC.

signalling.question: Was the reference appropriate for connectivity analysis?
signalling.quote: The EEG data in our study were recorded with reference electrode located near the Fpz location, which is not a typical reference for connectivity analysis.

signalling.question: Was EMG contamination of the gamma range controlled?
signalling.quote: This is particularly important for γ range activity, which may be significantly contaminated by tonic EMG activity (Whitham et al., 2008, Whitham et al., 2007), which is expected to have a global impact.

signalling.question: Was test-retest reliability of the connectivity measures reported?
signalling.quote: Searched Sections 2.3, 2.4 and 4.4 for reliability or repeatability of COH/PCOH; none reported (the parameter investigation is in supplementary material not in the document).

domains.rationale:
The cluster-based permutation test (Maris and Oostenveld) is appropriate in principle for controlling multiplicity across channels and frequencies. Several problems weaken the cited result:
- The cluster-forming threshold, number of permutations, test statistic and channel neighbourhood are not reported.
- Four cluster tests are reported (lCEC, lCEO, lPEC, lPEO) with no correction across them.
- The test was introduced 'as a more powerful method' after the uncorrected, FDR-corrected and global analyses failed.
- The authors call the study exploratory.
- The reference choice was kept partly because alternatives 'adversely affected the statistical results'.
- The PSD comparator null is reported with no test statistics. It was tested band-averaged, not with the same cluster approach, so the index and comparator measures were tested at unequal sensitivity.
This reads as analytic flexibility with incomplete reporting rather than an inappropriate method, so the answer is Unclear, not No.

signalling.question: Was the analysis used for the cited result appropriate for multiplicity across channels and frequencies?
signalling.quote: At the last part of our analysis we use cluster-based permutation tests (Maris and Oostenveld, 2007) to overcome the multiple comparisons problem.

signalling.question: Were the parameters of the cluster-based permutation test reported?
signalling.quote: Searched Sections 2.4.3 and 3.5 and the Fig. 9 caption for the cluster-forming threshold, number of permutations, cluster statistic and channel adjacency; none are given.

signalling.question: Was the cluster analysis pre-specified rather than chosen after corrected tests failed?
signalling.quote: The above statistical results, unfortunately, do not survive FDR correction (smallest corrected p-value was 0.1429). ... we perform cluster-based permutation tests as a more powerful method to compare the local connectivity of the two subject groups.

signalling.question: Was the study framed as confirmatory?
signalling.quote: we initially treat our study as exploratory, keep the uncorrected p-values and partially comment on how the results change after False Discovery Rate correction

signalling.question: Was multiplicity across the four cluster tests (two measures by two eye conditions) addressed?
signalling.quote: Fig. 9 presents the channel/frequency clusters that are identified. (No correction across the four metric-condition tests is described.)

signalling.question: Were analytic choices made independently of the results?
signalling.quote: Mastoid electrodes were not available to re-reference to linked mastoids, and re-referencing to Cz or average reference adversely affected the statistical results.

signalling.question: Was the group-comparison test suited to the data?
signalling.quote: statistical comparison of the two subject groups (MCI vs CN) is done with Welch’s two-sample t-test (Ruxton, 2006) which is appropriate for unequal variances and imbalanced data sets.

signalling.question: Was the comparator (PSD) tested with reported statistics and a comparable method?
signalling.quote: Statistical analysis of the PSD averaged in each band did not indicate any significant difference.

overall: Some concerns (JBI analytical cross-sectional: items 6, 7 and 8 Unclear; items 1 to 5 Yes)
overall_rationale:
By the review's JBI rule, no item among confounder identification, confounder strategy, valid outcome measurement and appropriate analysis is 'No', so the rating is not high. Three of these items are Unclear, so it is not low.
- Confounding: adjustment for the large age and education imbalance is claimed for the t-tests but not shown, and is not stated for the cited cluster tests.
- Outcome measurement: gamma-range scalp PCOH was measured with an atypical reference, no EMG-specific removal, retained blinks, and manual segment selection with no reported blinding.
- Analysis: the cluster test is appropriate in principle, but its parameters are unreported. It was introduced after the corrected analyses failed, it is one of four uncorrected cluster tests, and the PSD comparator was tested with a less sensitive, unreported method.
Participant definition and diagnostic classification are sound, and the requirement for two consecutive stable diagnoses is a strength.
